correctness.rationale: Nondegeneracy makes multiplication equivalent to a nonsingular orthogonally diagonalizable symmetric binary B. Each nonisotropic projective line L has a distinct complementary L-perp; counting the m=q+1-epsilon lines and vector scalings gives m(q-1)^2 ordered bases and m/2 classes. Exactly the single pair containing square generator ku is sparse when B(u,u)≠0, giving support-one probability 2/m. Epsilon is 1 for q even and 0/2 for q odd, so uniqueness iff q2 or split q3. Independent direct field enumeration of diagonal nondegenerate forms over F2,F3,F5,F7 reproduces counts and graphs.

evidence: General natural-family geometry and algebra classifications encompass binary forms but do not supply these all-q finite exact probabilities.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The old unrestricted uniqueness criterion is actually false at |F|=2 and split |F|=3 because its proof assumes >3 elements; the present exact finite-field boundary does not follow from that incorrect unrestricted statement.
